question:
A 76-year-old woman comes to the clinic reporting one week of suicidal thoughts. Her history includes
depression, which began after her husband’s death in a motor vehicle accident seven years ago. At
that time, she attempted suicide by overdosing on over-the-counter pills but made a full recovery. Her
depression had been well-managed with sertraline until this past week. She also has a history of
hypertension, controlled with hydrochlorothiazide. The patient is retired, lives alone, enjoys gardening,
and participates in activities at her local community center. Upon further questioning, she states she
has no specific plan but discloses that she purchased a gun two years ago. She denies tobacco,
alcohol, or drug use. Which of the following represents this patient’s most significant risk factor for
completed suicide? Answer Choices: (A) Social isolation (B) History of depression (C) Elderly age (D)
Advanced age (E) Recent loss of spouse (F) Previous attempt (G) Lack of current plan (H) Firearm
possession (I) Female gender (J) Living alone
 A. Recent loss of spouse
B. Social isolation
C. Lack of current plan
D. Advanced age
E. Female gender

F. History of depression
G. Firearm possession
H. Elderly age
I. Living alone
J. Previous attempt
